Surat al-Jumu'ah is Madani according to all scholars, and it has eleven verses. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best day on which the sun has risen is the day of Friday. On it Adam was created, on it he was admitted into Paradise, on it he was removed from it, and the Hour will not come except on a Friday." And from him (Abu Hurairah) he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We are the last (in time) and the first (in rank) on the Day of Resurrection, and we are the first to enter Paradise, except that they were given the Book before us, and we were given it after them. Then they differed, and Allah guided us to the truth about which they differed. This is their day about which they differed, and Allah guided us to it." He said: "The day of Friday. So today is ours, tomorrow is for the Jews, and the day after tomorrow is for the Christians."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah, the King, the Holy One, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ (1)

The discussion of this has already passed. Abu al-'Aliyah and Nasr ibn 'Asim recited "al-Malik al-Quddus al-'Aziz al-Hakim" all in the nominative (raf'), meaning: He is the King.

He said: ﴿It is He who sent among the unlettered a messenger from among them﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "The unlettered (al-ummiyyun) are all the Arabs, whether or not they could write, because they were not People of the Book (ahl al-kitab)." It was also said: "The unlettered are those who do not write." This was the case with Quraysh. Mansur narrated from Ibrahim that he said: "The unlettered (ummi) is one who can read but cannot write." This has already been discussed in "al-Baqarah" [see vol. 2, pp. 5 and 136].

﴿A messenger from among them﴾ refers to Muhammad (ﷺ). There is no Arab tribe (hayy) without a kinship tie to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) among them, for they gave birth to him. Ibn Ishaq said: "The exception is the tribe of Taghlib, for Allah purified His Prophet (ﷺ) from them because of their Christianity, so they had no lineage claim over him." He was unlettered and did not read from any book, nor did he learn (ﷺ).

al-Mawardi said: If it is asked, "What is the point of the favour if He sent an unlettered prophet?" the answer has three aspects. First, it agrees with what the prophets had foretold in their good tidings. Second, it matches their own condition, so it is closer to being acceptable to them. Third, it removes any suspicion regarding his teaching of what he called to from the books he had read and the wisdom he recited. I say: all of this is evidence of his miracle and the truthfulness of his prophethood.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿He recites to them His verses﴾ means the Qur'an. ﴿And purifies them﴾ means He makes them pure of heart through faith, as Ibn 'Abbas said. It was also said: He cleanses them from the filth of disbelief and sins, as Ibn Jurayj and Muqatil said. al-Suddi said: He takes the zakat (obligatory alms) of their wealth. ﴿And teaches them the Book﴾ means the Qur'an, ﴿and the wisdom﴾ means the Sunnah (the prophetic practice), as al-Hasan said. Ibn 'Abbas said: "The Book" means writing with the pen, because writing spread among the Arabs through the Law when they were commanded to fix it in writing. Malik ibn Anas said: "The wisdom" means fiqh (jurisprudence) in religion. This matter has already been discussed in "al-Baqarah" [see vol. 2, pp. 5 and 136].

﴿And indeed they had been before in manifest error﴾: that is, before him, and before he was sent to them.

﴿In manifest error﴾ means they were in a state of going astray from the truth.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 62, verse 3:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And others among them﴾ is a conjunction (ʿataf) upon "al-ummiyyin" (the unlettered), meaning: He was sent to the unlettered and He was sent to others among them. It is also permissible that it be in the accusative by conjunction upon the hā' and mīm in "yuʿallimuhum wa-yuzakkihim," meaning: He teaches them and teaches others among the believers, because teaching, when it continues until the end of time, is all attributed to its first source, so it is as if he is the one who undertook everything that came about from him.

(﴿Who have not yet joined them﴾) meaning: they were not in their time, and they will come after them. Said Ibn ʿAmr Saʿid ibn Jubayr: they are the non-Arabs (ʿajam). In Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: "We were sitting with the Prophet (ﷺ) when the surah "al-Jumuʿah" was revealed to him. When he recited ﴿And others among them who have not yet joined them﴾, a man said: 'Who are these, O Messenger of Allah?' The Prophet (ﷺ) did not respond to him until he asked once, twice, or three times." He said: "Salman al-Farisi was among us." He said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) placed his hand upon Salman, then said: 'If faith were at the Pleiades, men from these would reach it.'" In another narration: "If religion were at the Pleiades, a man from Persia – or he said, from the sons of Persia – would take it," the wording of Muslim, until he reaches it.

ʿIkrimah said: they are the Tabiʿun (the Successors). Mujahid said: they are all people, meaning those after the Arabs among whom Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent. This was also said by Ibn Zayd and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. The two said: they are those who entered Islam after the Prophet (ﷺ) until the Day of Resurrection. Sahl ibn Saʿd al-Saʿidi narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, in the loins of my Ummah are men and women who will enter Paradise without reckoning" – then he recited: ﴿And others among them who have not yet joined them﴾. The first opinion is the more established. It has also been narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I saw myself giving drink to black sheep, then I followed them with white-spotted sheep; interpret them, O Abu Bakr." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, as for the black ones, they are the Arabs, and as for the white-spotted ones, they are the non-Arabs who follow you after the Arabs." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "So the angel interpreted them" – meaning Jibril, peace be upon him. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Layla from a man among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), who was ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him).

Ibn 'Abbas said: "[It is] when He joined the non-Arabs (al-'ajam) with the Quraysh." It was also said that it means Islam: ﴿the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills﴾. This was said by al-Kalbi. It was said that it means revelation and prophethood, and this was said by Muqatil. A fourth view is that it is wealth spent in obedience to Allah, and this is the meaning of the statement of Abu Salih.

Muslim related from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, that the poor among the emigrants (fuqara' al-Muhajirin) came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "The people of wealth (ahl al-dutur) have taken the high ranks and lasting bliss." He said: "And what is that?" They said: "They pray as we pray, they fast as we fast, and they give charity while we do not give charity, and they free slaves while we do not free slaves." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I not teach you something by which you can overtake those who preceded you and get ahead of those who come after you, and no one will be more excellent than you except one who does the same as what you have done?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Glorify (Allah), exalt Him, and praise Him, thirty-three times after each prayer." Abu Salih said: The poor among the emigrants returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Our brothers, the people of wealth, have heard what we did, so they did the same." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills﴾.

A fifth view is that it is the people's submission to accepting the Prophet (ﷺ), their entry into his religion, and their support of him.

And Allah knows best.

This verse was revealed about the Jews when they abandoned acting on the Torah and did not believe in Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿Those who were charged with the Torah﴾ means they were obligated to act upon it, according to Ibn 'Abbas. Al-Jurjani said: it comes from *al-ḥamāla* (bearing, carrying responsibility), in the sense of *al-kafāla* (guarantee), meaning they took on the rulings of the Torah as a responsibility.

﴿Like the example of a donkey carrying books﴾. *Asfār* is the plural of *sifr*, which is a large book, because it reveals (*yusfiru*) its meaning when it is read. Maymun ibn Mihran said: The donkey does not know whether there is a book (*sifr*) on its back or a bag of dung (*zabīl*). The same is true of the Jews. In this there is a warning from Allah, exalted is He, to whoever carries the Book that he should learn its meanings and understand what is in it, lest he suffer the blame that befell those people.

The poet said:
They are beasts of burden for books, having no knowledge of them,
and their good is nothing but the knowledge of camels.

By your life, the camel does not know, when it sets out in the morning,
with its loads, or when it returns, what is in the sacks.

Yahya ibn Yaman said: One of them writes down a hadith without understanding it or reflecting on it, and when someone asks him about a question, he sits like a man who is a scribe (*mukātab*).

The poet said:
Indeed the narrators, in ignorance of what they carry,
are like camels, upon which the ... is loaded.
Neither does the ... benefit from the camels carrying it,
nor do the camels benefit from carrying the ...

Mundhir ibn Sa'id al-Ballūṭī, may Allah have mercy on him, said, and excelled:
Cry out with whatever you wish, you will find supporters,
and tie up books, you will find a donkey.
It carries what you have put of books;
it carries them like the example of the donkey.
It carries books for it, and does not know
whether what is in them is correct or mistaken.[Thus it stands in the manuscripts, with this addition by which the metre is kept. It may be that the correct reading is: "Whether what is in them is pearls or dust," where *jumān* (with a damma) means pearls, and *burā* means dust.]
If they are questioned, they say: "Thus we have narrated,
we have not lied and we have not transgressed."
Their elder becomes small in the assembly,
because he has imitated the people of ignorance.[In one copy: "qadar" (instead of "qallada").]

Then ﴿they did not carry it﴾, meaning they did not act upon it. He likened them, while the Torah was in their hands and they did not act by it, to a donkey carrying books, having nothing but the weight of the load without any benefit. *Yaḥmilu* is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (*ḥāl*), meaning "carrying." It may also be in the genitive position as a descriptive attribute (*wasf*), because the donkey is like the base person. The poet said:
And I pass by the base person who insults me,
so I turn away and say: "It does not concern me."[The completion of the line is: "so I turn away and say: 'It does not concern me.'"]

﴿Evil is the example of the people﴾: the example we have set forth for them. The word *mathal* has been elided (the genitive noun *mithl* has been omitted).

﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾, meaning those whom it has preceded in His knowledge that they will be disbelievers.

When the Jews claimed superiority and said, "We are the sons of God and His beloved" [Al-Ma'idah: 18], Allah the Exalted said: "If you claim that you are the friends of Allah to the exclusion of other people, then for the friends of Allah with Him is honour."

﴿So wish for death, if you are truthful﴾, so that you may arrive at what the friends of Allah arrive at. ﴿But they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent ahead﴾, i.e., they have advanced it through denying Muhammad (ﷺ). So if they had wished it, they would have died, and in that would be the refutation of their claim and of the guardianship they asserted.

In a hadith, when this verse was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, if they wished for death, not a Jew left upon the face of the earth would not die." In this is a report of the unseen and a miracle of the Prophet (ﷺ). The meaning of this verse has passed in al-Baqarah, in His saying: ﴿Say: If the Last Abode with Allah is yours exclusively, to the exclusion of other people, then wish for death, if you are truthful﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 94] [See vol. 2, p. 33].

Al-Zajjaj said: One does not say "inna Zaydan fa-muntaliq" (Indeed Zayd, so he is departing), but here He says: ﴿fa-innahu mulaqikum﴾ ("then indeed it will meet you"), because of what is in the meaning of "alladhi" (the one who) of conditional and consequent. That is, "if you flee from it, then indeed it will meet you." This is an emphatic way of indicating that fleeing from it benefits nothing. Zuhayr said:

Whoever shuns the causes of death, they will overtake him,
even if he tries to climb the causes of the sky with a ladder.

I say: It is also permissible that the sentence be complete at His saying ﴿alladhi tafirruna minhu﴾ ("the death from which you flee"), and then begin with ﴿fa-innahu mulaqikum﴾. Tarafa said:

And death is sufficient as a preacher, know this well,
for the one upon whom death has been decreed.

So remember death and beware of mentioning it,
for indeed in death there are lessons for the people of understanding.

Everything will one day meet its doom,
whether in a settled place or on the back of a journey.

And the fates surround him, watching him,
and caution does not save him from death.

In it there are thirteen issues.

**The first issue:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, when the call is made for the prayer on the day of Friday (al-jumu'ah)...﴾. Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, al-A'mash and others read (al-jum'ah) with the *mim* sukun, as a lightened form. Both are dialects, and their plurals are *jum'ah* and *jumu'at*. Al-Farra' said: it is said *al-jum'ah* (with sukun on the *mim*), *al-juma'ah* (with damma on the *mim*) and *al-jamu'ah* (with fatha on the *mim*), in which case it is an attribute of the day, meaning that it gathers the people, as one says *dahkah* for one who laughs a great deal. Ibn Abbas said: the Qur'an was revealed with the heavy and emphatic form, so recite it *jumu'ah*, meaning with damma on the *mim*. Al-Farra' and Abu Ubayd said: the lightened form is more analogous and better, like *ghurfah* and *ghurf*, *tur fah* and *turf*, and *hujrah* and *hujar*. Fatha on the *mim* is the dialect of the Banu Aqil. It was also said that it is the dialect of the Prophet ﷺ. It is related from Salman that the Prophet ﷺ said: "It was only named *Jumu'ah* because Allah gathered in it the creation of Adam." It was also said: because Allah finished in it the creation of everything, so the created things were gathered in it. It was said: so that the congregations might gather in it. It was said: because the people gather in it for the prayer. *Min* here means *fi* (in), i.e. on the day, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Show me what they have created from the earth﴾ [Fatir: 40], meaning "in the earth."

**The second issue:** Abu Salamah said: the first to say "Amma ba'd" was Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy, and he was the first to name Friday *Jumu'ah*. Friday used to be called *al-'Arubah*. It was also said: the first to name it *Jumu'ah* were the Ansar.

Ibn Sirin said: the people of Medina gathered before the Prophet ﷺ came to Medina and before the Friday prayer was revealed, and they were the ones who named it *al-Jumu'ah*. That is because they said: the Jews have a day on which they gather every seven days, which is Saturday, and the Christians have a similar day, which is Sunday. Come, let us gather so that we may make a day for ourselves on which we remember Allah and pray and remind one another, or as they said. They said: Saturday is for the Jews and Sunday for the Christians, so make it the day of *al-'Arubah*. So they gathered to As'ad ibn Zurarah (Abu Umamah, may Allah be pleased with him), and he led them in two rak'ahs that day and admonished them. They named it the day of *al-Jumu'ah* when they gathered. As'ad slaughtered a sheep for them, and they ate their evening and midday meals from it because of their small number. This was the first Friday prayer in Islam.

I say: it is also related that they were twelve men, as will come. In this report it is mentioned that the one who gathered them and led them in prayer was As'ad ibn Zurarah, and likewise in the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik from his father Ka'b, as will come.

Al-Bayhaqi said: we have also related from Musa ibn Uqbah, from Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, that Mus'ab ibn Umayr was the first to hold the Friday prayer in Medina for the Muslims, before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to it. Al-Bayhaqi said: it is possible that Mus'ab led them in it with the help of As'ad ibn Zurarah, so Ka'b attributed it to him. And Allah knows best.

As for the first Friday prayer the Prophet ﷺ held with his Companions, the people of biography and history said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived as an emigrant and stopped at Quba, among the Banu Amr ibn Awf, on Monday, twelve nights having passed of the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, when the forenoon had become strong. From that year the calendar is counted. He remained at Quba until Thursday and founded their mosque. Then on Friday he went out to Medina, and Friday overtook him among the Banu Salim ibn Awf, in the bottom of a valley of theirs where the people had taken a mosque at that place. He led them in the prayer and gave the sermon. This was the first sermon he gave in Medina, and in it he said:

"All praise is for Allah. I praise Him, seek His help, seek His forgiveness, and seek His guidance. I believe in Him and do not disbelieve in Him, and I am hostile to whoever disbelieves in Him. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and messenger. He sent him with guidance, the religion of truth, light, admonition and wisdom, after a gap in the messengers, a scarcity of knowledge, the straying of people, the cutting off of time, the nearness of the Hour, and the closeness of the term. Whoever obeys Allah and His messenger has been guided rightly, and whoever disobeys Allah and His messenger has gone astray, has fallen short, and has strayed far. I enjoin you to fear Allah, for it is the best thing a Muslim can enjoin upon a Muslim: that he urge him toward the Hereafter and command him to fear Allah. Beware of what Allah has warned you of concerning Himself, for the fear of Allah on the part of one who acts upon it with dread and awe of his Lord is a true help for what you seek of the matter of the Hereafter. Whoever sets right what is between him and his Lord regarding his affairs, in private and in public, intending by it only the face of Allah, will have a remembrance in his immediate affairs and a store for what comes after death, when a man will be in need of what he has sent forward. As for what is other than that, he will wish that between himself and it there were a great distance. Allah warns you of Himself, and Allah is Kind to the servants."

[Al Imran: 30]. He is the one who has fulfilled His word and accomplished His promise, and there is no changing of that, for He says, exalted is He: ﴿The word is not changed with Me, and I am not unjust to the servants﴾ [Qaf: 29]. So fear Allah concerning your immediate affairs and your later ones, in private and in public, for ﴿whoever fears Allah, He will remove from him his misdeeds and enlarge his reward﴾ [al-Talaq: 5]. ﴿Whoever fears Allah has achieved a great success.﴾ The fear of Allah is protection from His hatred, from His punishment and from His wrath. The fear of Allah whitens faces, pleases the Lord and raises the rank. So take your share and do not neglect your duty toward Allah, for He has taught you His Book and laid out for you His path, ﴿so that He may know those who are truthful and may know the liars﴾. So do good as Allah has done good to you, be hostile to His enemies, and strive for Allah with the striving that is due to Him. He has chosen you and named you Muslims, ﴿that whoever perishes might perish by clear evidence, and whoever lives might live by clear evidence﴾. There is no power and no strength except through Allah. So remember Allah often and work for what comes after death, for whoever sets right what is between him and Allah, Allah will suffice him for what is between him and the people. That is because Allah decides over the people and they cannot decide over Him, and He possesses the people and they do not possess Him. Allah is greatest, and there is no power and no strength except through Allah, the Most High, the Mighty."

The first Friday prayer held after that was in a village called "Juwathi," one of the villages of Bahrain. It was also said that the first to name it *al-Jumu'ah* was Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy ibn Ghalib, because Quraysh gathered to Ka'b, as has been mentioned. And Allah knows best.

**The third issue:** Allah addressed the believers with the Friday prayer and not the disbelievers, as an honour and a dignity for them, saying: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, and then singled them out with the call. Although it is included in the general meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when you call to the prayer﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 58], this is to show its obligation and the emphasis of its duty. Some scholars said: that the prayer here is the Friday prayer is known by consensus, not from the wording itself. Ibn al-Arabi said: in my view it is known from the wording itself through a subtle point, which is His saying "on the day of Friday," and that indicates it, because the call that is specific to that day is the call to that prayer. As for other than it, it is general across all days. If the intended meaning were not the call to Friday, its specification with that day and its attachment to it would have no meaning and no benefit.

**The fourth issue:** The ruling on the call to prayer (adhan) has already been covered fully in surah al-Ma'idah. In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the call was as for the other prayers: one caller called when the Prophet ﷺ sat on the pulpit (minbar). Abu Bakr, Umar and Ali at Kufa did likewise. Then Uthman added a third call on the pulpit, [note: it is the first in time at the zenith, and called third because it was added before the iqamah]... on his house called al-Zawra', when the people in Medina had become numerous. When they heard it they came, and when Uthman sat on the pulpit the caller of the Prophet ﷺ called, then Uthman gave the sermon. Ibn Majah recorded it in his Sunan from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, from al-Sa'ib ibn Yazid, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had only one caller; when he went out he called, and when he came down he began the iqamah. Abu Bakr and Umar were likewise. When Uthman came to power and the people became numerous, he added the third call on a house in the market called al-Zawra'; when he went out he called, and when he came down he began the iqamah. Al-Bukhari recorded it through several chains with the same meaning. In some of the reports it is stated that the second call on Friday was ordered by Uthman ibn Affan when the people of the mosque became numerous, and the call on Friday used to be made when the imam sat down.

Al-Mawardi said: as for the first call, it is an innovation which Uthman ibn Affan did so that the people might prepare themselves to attend the sermon when Medina had grown and its population increased. Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, had ordered the call to be made in the market before the mosque, so that the people would leave their trading; when they had gathered, the call was made in the mosque. Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, made it two calls in the mosque.

Ibn al-Arabi said: and in the sound hadith, the call was one in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When it was the time of Uthman, he added the third call at al-Zawra'. He called it "third" in the hadith because he attached it to the iqamah, as the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Between every two calls there is a prayer for whoever wills," meaning the call and the iqamah. People suppose that it is an original call, so they made the callers three, which was an error, and then they gathered them at one time, which was an error upon an error. I have seen them call in the city of peace (Madinat al-Salam) after the call from the minaret, in front of the imam beneath the pulpit, in a congregation, as they used to do among us in the past dynasties. All of that is an innovation.

**The fifth issue:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿then hasten to the remembrance of Allah﴾. The scholars differed about the meaning of "hasten" (al-sa'y) here, in three views. The first: it means intending. Al-Hasan said: by Allah, it is not walking on foot, but hastening with the hearts and the intention. The second: it means action, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it its striving, while being a believer﴾ [al-Isra': 19], and His saying: ﴿Indeed your efforts are diverse﴾ [al-Layl: 4], and His saying: ﴿And that man will have only what he strives for﴾ [al-Najm: 39]. This is the view of the majority. Zuhayr said:

*"After them a people strove to reach them,*
*but they did not act, nor were they blamed, nor did they falter."*

And he also said:

*"Ghayz ibn Murrah strove, the striver,*
*after the bond between the clan had been split with blood."*

[In the commentary on Zuhayr's Diwan: "the two strivers" are al-Harith ibn Awf and Harim ibn Sinan, who strove in the blood-money. It was also said: Kharijah ibn Sinan and al-Harith ibn Awf; "sa'a" means did a good deed. "Ghayz ibn Murrah" is a clan of Ghatafan ibn Sa'd. "Tabazzala bi'l-dam" means split open. He says: there was a truce between them, which was split open by blood. He says: they strove after it was split, so they made peace.]

That is, act by proceeding toward the remembrance of God, and occupy yourselves with its means: ritual washing, purification, and turning towards it. The third view is that what is meant is walking on foot. That is a virtue, but it is not a condition. In al-Bukhari it is related that Abu 'Abs ibn Jabr, whose name was 'Abd al-Rahman and who was one of the senior Companions, walked to the Friday prayer on foot and said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "Whoever has his feet covered with dust in the way of God, God will forbid him to the Fire." The apparent meaning may also allow a fourth view, which is running and hastening. Ibn al-'Arabi said: this is what the most knowledgeable Companions and the earliest jurists rejected. 'Umar recited it as "fa-amdu ila dhikri Allah" (then proceed to the remembrance of God), to avoid the path of running and hastening that the apparent sense indicates. Ibn Mas'ud also recited it in this way and said: "If I had recited fa-s'aw, I would have run until my cloak fell off." Ibn Shihab recited: "fa-amdu ila dhikri Allah, sailan tilka al-sabil" (proceeding to the remembrance of God, taking that path). All of this is their tafsir (exegesis), not a recitation of the revealed Qur'an. It is permissible to recite the Qur'an with tafsir in the context of explanation.

Abu Bakr al-Anbari said: Those who opposed the Mushaf (the codified text) have argued from the recitation of 'Umar and Ibn Mas'ud, and that Kharasha ibn al-Hurr said: 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, saw me with a piece (of parchment) in which was "fa-s'aw ila dhikri Allah," and 'Umar said to me: "Who taught you this?" I said: "Ubayy." He said: "Ubayy is the best of us in reciting the abrogated (text)." Then 'Umar recited "fa-amdu ila dhikri Allah." Idris narrated to us, saying: Khalaf narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from al-Mughira, from Ibrahim, from Kharasha, and he mentioned it. And Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us: Muhammad, who is Ibn Sa'dan, informed us, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, who said: "I never heard 'Umar recite except 'fa-amdu ila dhikri Allah.'" And Idris informed us, saying: Khalaf narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from al-Mughira, from Ibrahim, that 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud recited "fa-amdu ila dhikri Allah" and said: "If it were fa-s'aw, I would have run until my cloak fell off." Abu Bakr said: He was refuted by the fact that the community unanimously agreed on fa-s'aw, which is transmitted from God, the Lord of the worlds, and from His Messenger (ﷺ). As for 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, "fa-amdu" is not authentically transmitted from him, because the chain is not continuous, since Ibrahim al-Nakha'i did not hear anything from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud. Rather, "fa-amdu" is transmitted from 'Umar, may God be pleased with him. When someone alone reports something that contradicts the verse and the consensus, that is a lapse of memory on his part. The Arabs agree that sa'y (striving/going) comes in the sense of proceeding, though it is not free of earnestness and exertion. Zuhayr said:

"He strove, striving with anger, after
he had spent between the clans with blood."

He meant by sa'y proceeding with earnestness and exertion, and did not intend running or quickening the stride. Al-Farra' and Abu 'Ubayda said: the meaning of sa'y in the verse is proceeding. Al-Farra' argued from their saying: "He strives in the lands seeking God's bounty," meaning he proceeds with earnestness and diligence. Abu 'Ubayda argued from the words of the poet:

"I strive over the majority of Banu Malik,
every man is a striver in his own affair."

Could sa'y in this verse bear any meaning other than proceeding with exertion? And it is impossible that this meaning would be hidden from Ibn Mas'ud, despite his eloquence and mastery of Arabic. I say: Among what shows that running is not what is meant here is his saying, peace be upon him: "When the prayer is established, do not come to it running, but come to it walking, and upon you is tranquillity." Al-Hasan said: "By God, it does not mean walking on foot. They were only forbidden to come to the prayer except with tranquillity and dignity upon them, but it means with the hearts, the intention, and humility." Qatada said: "Sa'y is that you strive with your heart and your deeds." This is good, for it combines the three views. Hadiths have come concerning washing for Friday, perfuming, and adorning oneself with clothing, which are mentioned in the books of hadith.

The sixth matter: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe﴾ is an address to the responsible adults by consensus. Excluded from it, by evidence, are the sick, the chronically disabled, travellers, slaves, and women. According to Abu Hanifa, the blind and the old man who cannot walk except with a guide are also excluded. Abu al-Zubayr narrated from Jabir that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, the Friday (prayer) is obligatory upon him on Friday, except a sick person, or a traveller, or a woman, or a child, or a slave. Whoever is occupied with amusement or trade, God will be independent of him, and God is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy." Al-Daraqutni transmitted it. Our scholars, may God have mercy on them, said: No one who is obliged to attend the Friday prayer may stay away from it except for an excuse that prevents him from coming to it, such as a restraining illness, or fear of the worsening of an illness, or fear of oppression by the ruler against him in property or body, short of a judgment against him with right. Heavy rain with mud is an excuse, if it does not cease. Malik did not consider it an excuse for him, as related by al-Mahdawi. If someone stayed away from it because of a close relative who was a guardian and was dying, with no one present to attend to his affair, he hoped that he would be within leeway. Ibn 'Umar did this.

Whoever stays away from it without an excuse and prays before the imam must repeat the prayer, and it is not sufficient for him to pray before him. In his staying away from it while being able to attend, he is disobedient to God by his action. The seventh matter: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿when it is called for prayer﴾ specifies that the obligation of the Friday prayer applies to the one near enough to hear the call. As for the one whose home is far away and who cannot hear the call, he does not fall under the address. Scholars differed regarding those who come to the Friday prayer from near and far. Ibn 'Umar, Abu Hurayra, and Anas said: the Friday prayer is obligatory on those within the city (miṣr) up to six miles. Rabi'a said: four miles. Malik and al-Layth said: three miles. Al-Shafi'i said: the standard for hearing the adhan is that the muezzin should be loud (ṣayyit, one whose voice is strong and high), the sounds should be calm, the wind still, and the muezzin's position should be at the wall of the town. In the Sahih it is related from 'A'isha that people used to come to the Friday prayer in turns from their homes and from al-'Awali, coming in the dust (the reading in some manuscripts is "al-'aba'", pl. of 'aba'a), and the dust would reach them, so sweat would come from them. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "If only you had washed on this day." Our scholars said: When the voice is strong and people are in quiet and stillness, the farthest reach of sound is three miles. Al-'Awali of Medina, the nearest of them, is three miles away. Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Ishaq said: the Friday prayer is obligatory on whoever hears the call. Al-Daraqutni transmitted from the hadith of 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who said: "The Friday prayer is only for the one who hears the call." Abu Hanifa and his companions said: it is obligatory on those within the city, whether they hear the call or not, and it is not obligatory on those outside the city even if they hear the call. He was asked: Is the Friday prayer obligatory on the people of Zabara, between which and Kufa is the course of a river? He said: No. It is also reported from Rabi'a: that it is obligatory on one who, when he hears the call and leaves his house walking, reaches the prayer. It is also reported from al-Zuhri that it is obligatory upon him if he hears the adhan.

The eighth matter: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿When it is called for prayer on the day of Friday, then strive to the remembrance of God﴾ is evidence that the Friday prayer is obligatory only upon the call, and the call only occurs when the time has come, by the evidence of his saying, peace be upon him: "When the prayer is present, call the adhan, then the iqama, and let the older of you lead." He said this to Malik ibn al-Huwayrith and his companion. In al-Bukhari it is related from Anas ibn Malik that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to pray the Friday prayer when the sun declined. It is also reported from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and Ahmad ibn Hanbal that it is prayed before the decline (zawal). Ahmad relied on this in the hadith of Salama ibn al-Akwa': "We used to pray with the Prophet (ﷺ), then we would leave, and there was no shade for the walls." And by the hadith of Ibn 'Umar: "We did not take a midday rest or lunch except after the Friday prayer." The same is related from Sahl. Muslim transmitted it. The hadith of Salama is understood as referring to early performance. Hisham ibn 'Abd al-Malik narrated it from Ya'la ibn al-Harith, from Iyas ibn Salama ibn al-Akwa', from his father. Wakī' narrated from Ya'la, from Iyas, from his father, who said: "We used to hold the Friday prayer with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) when the sun declined, then we would return, seeking the shade." This is the position of the majority of later and earlier scholars, and it is analogous to the Zuhr prayer. The hadith of Ibn 'Umar and Sahl is evidence that they used to go early to the Friday prayer very early, at dawn or before it, so they did not take their midday rest or lunch except after the prayer was finished. Malik held that going early to the Friday prayer is only shortly before the decline. He interpreted the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever goes in the first hour, it is as if he has offered a camel..." — the whole hadith — as meaning that it was in one single hour. The rest of the scholars took it to mean the twelve temporal hours of the day, whether equal or varying according to the lengthening and shortening of the day. Ibn al-'Arabi said: This is more sound, based on the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may God be pleased with them both: "They did not take their midday rest or lunch except after the Friday prayer, because of their great earliness to it."

The ninth matter: God, Exalted is He, made the Friday prayer obligatory upon every Muslim, refuting those who say it is a collective obligation (fard kifaya), a view attributed to some Shafi'is. Some who did not verify have reported from Malik that it is a sunna. The majority of the community and the imams hold that it is an individual obligation (fard 'ayn), based on God's saying, Exalted is He: ﴿When it is called for prayer on the day of Friday, strive to the remembrance of God and leave off trading﴾. It is also firmly reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "People must stop neglecting the Friday congregations, or God will seal their hearts, and then they will surely be among the heedless." This is clear evidence for the obligation and the obligatory nature of the Friday prayer. In the Sunan of Ibn Majah, from Abu al-Ja'd al-Damari, who had companionship with the Prophet, he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever abandons the Friday prayer three times out of negligence toward it..."

ṬABA‘A Allāhu ʿalā qalbihi (. Its isnad is ṣaḥīḥ. And the ḥadīth of Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:) Whoever leaves the Friday prayer three times without a necessity, Allah seals his heart (. Ibn al-ʿArabī: And it is established from the Prophet ﷺ that he said:) Going to the Friday prayer is obligatory upon every Muslim (.

The Tenth Issue: Allah has made the going to the Friday prayer obligatory absolutely, without any condition. The condition of wuḍūʾ (ablution) is established by the Qur'an and the Sunnah for all prayers, based on His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿When you rise up to prayer, wash your faces﴾ [al-Mā'idah: 6], to the end of the verse [see vol. 6, p. 6]. And the Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah does not accept a prayer without purification." But a group went to an extreme and said: The ghusl (major ablution) of Friday is obligatory. Ibn al-ʿArabī: This is false, because al-Nasāʾī and Abū Dāwūd related in their Sunan that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever performs wuḍūʾ on Friday, then it is good and sufficient; and whoever performs ghusl, the ghusl is better." And in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever performs wuḍūʾ on Friday [[what is between the brackets is not found in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim.]] and does it well, then goes to the Friday prayer, listens attentively and remains silent, Allah forgives him what is between that Friday and the next Friday, and three additional days. And whoever touches the pebbles [[i.e., adjusts them for prostration] more than once during the prayer has engaged in idle conduct [[al-laghw: discourse that is cast off and worthless.]]." And this is an explicit text. In al-Muwaṭṭaʾ: that a man entered on a Friday while ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was delivering the khuṭbah... the ḥadīth [[The ḥadīth as it appears in al-Muwaṭṭaʾ and its commentary: "A man from among the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the mosque on a Friday while ʿUmar was delivering the khuṭbah. ʿUmar said: 'What hour is this?' (indicating that this hour is not among the hours of going to the Friday prayer, because it is a time when the scrolls have been folded). He said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, I returned from the marketplace, heard the call, and I did nothing more than perform wuḍūʾ' (an excuse that he did not occupy himself with anything other than the obligation, hastening to hear the khuṭbah and remembrance). ʿUmar said: 'Wuḍūʾ too! And you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command ghusl.'
(Its meaning: that together with what you missed of going early, you missed the virtue of the ghusl which you know the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command.)]] up to where he said: "I did nothing more than perform wuḍūʾ," so ʿUmar said: "Wuḍūʾ too? And you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command ghusl." So ʿUmar commanded him to perform ghusl [[In the originals: "fa-aqarra" with a qāf. The correction is from Ibn al-ʿArabī.]] and did not command him to return, which indicates that it is to be understood as recommended. It was not possible, since he had already engaged in the obligation—which is presence and attentive listening to the khuṭbah—that he should turn away from it to the Sunnah, and that was in the presence of the leading Companions and the senior Emigrants around ʿUmar, and in the mosque of the Prophet ﷺ.

The Eleventh Issue: The Friday prayer is not dropped because it falls on a day of ʿĪd. This is contrary to Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, for he said: When ʿĪd and Friday coincide, the obligation of the Friday prayer is dropped, due to the precedence of the ʿĪd over it and people being occupied with it instead of it. He relied in this on what is narrated: that ʿUthmān permitted the people of al-ʿAwālī [[al-ʿAwālī: places at the upper parts of Madinah's lands; the nearest of them is four miles from Madinah, and the farthest on the side of Najd is eight.]] on a day of ʿĪd to stay away from the Friday prayer. But the saying of one Companion is not a proof when it is opposed and it has not been agreed upon with it. The command to strive toward it applies on the day of ʿĪd just as it applies on all other days. In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite in the two ʿĪds and in the Friday prayer: "Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High" [al-Aʿlā: 1] and "Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming?" [al-Ghāshiyah: 1]. He said: And when ʿĪd and Friday coincided on one day, he would recite both of them in the two prayers as well. Related by Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Mājah.

The Twelfth Issue: The statement of the Exalted: ﴿to the remembrance of Allah﴾, meaning the prayer. It is also said: the khuṭbah and the admonitions; this was said by Saʿīd ibn Jubayr. Ibn al-ʿArabī: The correct view is that it is obligatory in all cases, and its beginning is the khuṭbah. This is what our scholars said, except ʿAbd al-Malik ibn al-Mājishūn, for he regarded it as a sunnah. The proof of its obligation is that it makes trade forbidden; had it not been obligatory, it would not have forbidden it, because a recommended act does not forbid what is permissible. And if we say that the remembrance means the prayer, then the khuṭbah is part of the prayer. And the servant may be a remembrer of Allah through his action just as he may be one who glorifies Allah through his action. Al-Zamakhsharī: If you say: How is the remembrance of Allah explained as the khuṭbah when it contains other things? I say: Whatever is a mention of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, praise of him and of his rightly-guided successors and of the pious believers, and admonition and reminder, is within the ruling of the remembrance of Allah. As for other than that, such as mentioning tyrants, their titles, praising them and supplicating for them, when they deserve the opposite, that is from the remembrance of Satan, and it is from the remembrance of Allah only in degrees.

The Thirteenth Issue: The statement of the Exalted: ﴿And leave off trade﴾. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prohibited it at the time of the Friday prayer, and He made it unlawful during its time for whoever is addressed with its obligation. Trade does not occur without buying, so He suffices by mentioning one of the two, as in His saying: ﴿garments that protect you from the heat and garments that protect you from your violence﴾ [al-Naḥl: 81] [see vol. 10, p. 160]. He specified trade because it is what the people of the markets are most occupied with. And whoever is not obliged to attend the Friday prayer is not forbidden from buying and selling.

Regarding the time of prohibition there are two views: it begins after the zawāl (midday) until the completion of the prayer; this was said by al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Ḥasan and ʿAṭāʾ. The second: from the time of the call to the khuṭbah until the time of the prayer; this was said by al-Shāfiʿī. The school of Mālik holds that trade is to be abandoned when the call to prayer is made, and what was concluded of such trade at that time is annulled according to him. But manumission, marriage, divorce and other things are not annulled, since it is not the custom of people to occupy themselves with them as they occupy themselves with trade. They said: Likewise partnership, gift and charity are rare and are not annulled. Ibn al-ʿArabī: The correct view is the annulment of all of them, because trade was forbidden only because of being occupied with it. So every contract that distracts from the Friday prayer, of all contracts, is prohibited by the Sharīʿah and annulled as a deterrent. Al-Mahdawī. Some scholars regarded trade during the stated time as permissible and interpreted the prohibition as recommendatory, and they cited His saying: ﴿That is better for you﴾. I say: This is the view of al-Shāfiʿī, for the sale is valid according to him and is not annulled. Al-Zamakhsharī said in his Tafsīr: Most scholars hold that this does not lead to the invalidity of the sale. They said: Because trade was not forbidden in its essence, but because of the distraction it causes from the obligation; so it is like prayer in usurped land, a usurped garment, and wuḍūʾ with usurped water. And some people held that it is invalid. I say: The correct view is its invalidity and its annulment, based on his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Every action upon which there is not our command is rejected," meaning, it is returned. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 62, verse 10:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then when the prayer has been concluded, disperse in the land﴾. This is a command of permission (amr ibahah), like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when you have come out of ihram, then hunt﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 2]. [[See vol. 6, p. 44]] It means: when you have finished the prayer, disperse in the land for trade and for attending to your needs.

(And seek of Allah's bounty) i.e., of His provision. ʿIrak ibn Malik, when he had prayed the Friday prayer, would leave and stand at the door of the mosque and say: "O Allah, I have answered Your call, performed Your obligation, and dispersed as You commanded me, so grant me of Your bounty, for You are the best of providers." Ja'far ibn Muhammad, regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And seek of Allah's bounty﴾, said: it is the work on the day of the sabab. And from al-Hasan ibn Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: the seeking of knowledge. It has also been said: voluntary prayer. And from Ibn ʿAbbas: they were not commanded to seek anything of the world; rather it is visiting the sick, attending funerals, and visiting a brother for the sake of Allah, exalted is He.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And remember Allah much﴾, i.e., with obedience and with the tongue, and with gratitude for what He has bestowed upon you of success in performing the obligatory duties.

(So that you may be successful) i.e., so that you may prosper. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: remembrance (dhikr) is obedience to Allah, exalted is He; whoever obeys Allah has remembered Him, and whoever does not obey Him is not a rememberer, even if he glorifies Allah often. This has already been mentioned as a marfu' report in "al-Baqarah" [[See vol. 2, p. 171]].

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 62, verse 11 (part 1 of 3):

There are seventeen issues (masa'il) in it.

The first: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when they see a trade or a diversion, they break away toward it﴾. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) was delivering the sermon standing on Friday, when a caravan (ʿir) [[al-ʿir, with a kasra on the ʿayn: camels carrying provisions, then applied to any caravan. Infalla al-nas: the people turned away.]] from al-Sham arrived, and the people turned away toward it until only twelve men remained, in one narration "I was among them." Then this verse was revealed concerning Friday: ﴿And when they see a trade or a diversion, they break away toward it, and leave you standing﴾. In another narration: "Among them were Abu Bakr and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both."

Al-Kalbi and others mentioned that the one who brought it was Dihyah ibn Khalifah al-Kalbi, coming from al-Sham, at a time of famine and high prices, and with him was everything the people needed of wheat, flour and other goods. He stopped at Ahjar al-Zayt [[Ahjar al-Zayt: a place in the market of Madinah.]] and beat the drum to announce his arrival to the people, so the people went out, except for twelve men. It was also said: eleven men. Al-Kalbi said: They were at the Friday sermon, and they broke away toward it, and eight men remained with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This was related by al-Tha'labi from Ibn 'Abbas.

Al-Daraqutni related from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: "While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was delivering the sermon to us on Friday, a caravan carrying food came and stopped at al-Baqi' [[al-Baqi': a cemetery in Madinah.]], so they turned toward it and broke away toward it, and left the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with only forty men, I being among them." He said: "Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿And when they see a trade or a diversion, they break away toward it, and leave you standing﴾."

Al-Daraqutni said: No one in this chain said "only forty men" except 'Ali ibn 'Asim from Husayn, and the companions of Husayn disagreed with him, saying: "There remained with the Prophet (ﷺ) only twelve men."

It is also related from him, upon him be prayers and peace, that he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if they had all gone out, Allah would have set the valley ablaze with fire upon them." This was mentioned by al-Zamakhshari.

A hadith in mursal form has been related listing the names of the twelve men, narrated by Asad ibn 'Amr, the father of Asad ibn Musa ibn Asad. In it: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was left with none except Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, Talhah, al-Zubayr, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, Sa'id ibn Zayd and Bilal, and 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud in one of the two narrations. In the other narration: 'Ammar ibn Yasir.

I say: He (the narrator) did not mention Jabir, yet Muslim mentioned that he was among them, and so did al-Daraqutni. So they would be thirteen. And if 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud was among them, they would be fourteen.

Abu Dawud, in his Maraseel, mentioned the reason why they permitted themselves to abandon listening to the sermon, although they were worthy, by their merit, of not doing so. He said: Mahmud ibn Khalid related to us, saying: al-Walid related to us, saying: Abu Mu'adh Bakr ibn Ma'ruf informed me that he heard Muqatil ibn Hayyan say: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pray the Friday prayer before the sermon, like the two 'Eids. Then one Friday, while the Prophet (ﷺ) was delivering the sermon, and he had already prayed the Friday prayer, a man entered and said: 'Dihyah ibn Khalifah al-Kalbi has arrived with merchandise,' and Dihyah, whenever he arrived, his people would receive him with tambourines (daffaf). So the people went out, and they did not think that there was any harm in abandoning the sermon. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And when they see a trade or a diversion, they break away toward it﴾. So the Prophet (ﷺ) brought the sermon forward on Friday and delayed the prayer. And no one would go out for a nosebleed or a discharge after the prohibition without asking the Prophet (ﷺ) permission, indicating to him with the finger next to the thumb; the Prophet (ﷺ) would grant him permission, and then he would gesture to him with his hand. Among the hypocrites was one for whom the sermon and sitting in the mosque were burdensome, and whenever a Muslim asked permission, the hypocrite would stand beside him, concealing himself with him until he left. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Allah already knows those of you who slip away, concealing themselves﴾ [al-Nur: 63], the verse."

Al-Suhayli said: Although this report has not been transmitted through a sound route, the good assumption about the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) necessitates that it is correct.

Qatadah said: "It has reached us that they did this three times, each time a caravan coming from al-Sham, and each of these coincided with a Friday." It was also said: their going out to the arrival of Dihyah al-Kalbi with his merchandise, and their looking at the caravan passing by, was a diversion with no benefit in it, except that it was of the kind that carries no sin if it occurred in another manner. But when abandoning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and breaking away from his presence became attached to it, it became grave and great, and there was revealed concerning it in the Qur'an what was revealed, and its disparagement by the name of diversion.

And there came from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Everything with which a man diverts himself is vain, except his shooting with his bow." The hadith.

It has already passed in Surah (al-Anfal)... So to Allah belongs all praise.

Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah said: "When the young women were married, they would pass by with flutes and drums, and the people would break away toward them, so this was revealed." And the pronoun was returned to the trade (tijarah) because it is more important. Talhah ibn Musarrif recited: "Wa-idha ra'aw al-tijara wa-al-lahwa infaddu ilayha" [with the verb's pronoun], i.e., "when they saw the trade and the diversion they broke away toward it."

It was also said: the meaning is "when they see a trade they break away toward it, or a diversion they break away toward it," and the second was omitted because the first indicates it, as the poet said:

We are with what we have, and you are with what you have, content, and the opinion differs.

It was also said: the better usage in Arabic is that the returning pronoun in the mention be made to refer to the last of the two nouns.

The second issue: The scholars differed about the number by which the Friday prayer is validly constituted (yan'aqid), in several views. Al-Hasan said: the Friday prayer is validly constituted with two. Al-Layth and Abu Yusuf said: with three. Sufyan al-Thawri and Abu Hanifah said: with four. Rabi'ah said: with twelve men.

Al-Najjad, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Sulayman [in some sources: "Sulayman"] mentioned, saying: Abu Khalid Yazid ibn al-Haytham ibn Tahman al-Daqqaq related to us, saying: Subh ibn Dinar related to us, saying: al-Mu'afa ibn 'Imran related to us, saying: Ma'qil ibn 'Ubayd Allah related to us, from al-Zuhri with his chain, to Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr: that the Prophet (ﷺ) sent him to Madinah, and that he stayed in the house of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, and led them in the Friday prayer, and they were twelve men; he slaughtered a sheep for them that day.

Al-Shafi'i said: with forty men.

Abu Ishaq al-Shirazi said in (Kitab al-Tanbih 'ala Madhhab al-Imam al-Shafi'i): Every village in which there are forty men who are adult, sane, free and resident, who do not travel away from it in summer or winter except for a necessary journey, and who are present from the beginning of the sermon until the Friday prayer is performed, the Friday prayer becomes obligatory upon them.

Ahmad and Ishaq inclined to this view, but they did not stipulate these conditions.

Malik said: If a village has a market and a mosque, then the Friday prayer is obligatory upon them without regard to number.

'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz wrote: Any village in which thirty houses have gathered, the Friday prayer is obligatory upon them.

Abu Hanifah said: The Friday prayer is not obligatory upon the people of the countryside and villages; it is not lawful for them to establish it there. What is stipulated for the obligation of the Friday prayer and its validity is: a congregational city (al-misr al-jami'), a ruling authority (al-sultan al-qahir), a standing market, and a flowing river.

He argued with the hadith of 'Ali: "There is no Friday prayer and no tashriq (Eid prayer) except in a congregational city (misr jami') and a company that assists them." [[What is between the two brackets is thus as it appears in the copies of the original.]] This is refuted by the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The first Friday prayer that was held after the Friday prayer in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in a village of the villages of Bahrain called Juwathi."

The argument of Imam al-Shafi'i regarding the forty is the hadith of Jabir mentioned above, which al-Daraqutni cited.

In the Sunan of Ibn Majah and also of al-Daraqutni, and in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi, on the authority of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, who said: "I was the guide of my father when his sight had gone. When I took him out to the Friday prayer and he heard the adhan, he would invoke blessings upon Abu Umamah and seek forgiveness for him." He said: "He continued like this for a time, whenever he heard the call to the Friday prayer he would do that. So I said to him: O father, your seeking forgiveness for Abu Umamah whenever you hear the call to the Friday prayer, what is it?" He said: "O my son, he was the first who held the Friday prayer in Madinah, in a hollow (hazm) of the Harrah of Banu Bayadah called Naqi' al-Khadimat." He said: I said: "How many were you that day?" He said: "Forty men." [[Al-hazm: what is level ground in the earth. Harrah Banu Bayadah: a village a mile from Madinah. Bayadah: a clan of the Ansar.]]

And Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah said: "The sunnah has passed that in every three there is an imam, and in every forty or more there is a Friday prayer, and Eid and Fitr, because they constitute a congregation." Al-Daraqutni recorded it.

Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Sulayman al-Najjad related: It was read to 'Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad al-Raqashi while I was listening: Raja' ibn Salamah related to me, saying: my father related to us, saying: Rawh ibn Ghutayf al-Thaqafi related to us, saying: al-Zuhri related to me, from Abu Salamah, who said: "I said to Abu Hurayrah: 'How many men make the Friday prayer obligatory?' He said: 'When the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reached fifty men, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) held the Friday prayer with them.'" It was read to 'Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad while I was listening, he said: Raja' ibn Salamah related to us, saying: 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad al-Muhallabi related to us, from Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Friday prayer is obligatory upon fifty men, and it is not obligatory upon fewer than that."

Ibn al-Mundhir said: 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz wrote: Whatever village in which fifty men gather, let them perform the Friday prayer.

Al-Zuhri related from Umm 'Abd Allah al-Dawsiyyah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Friday prayer is obligatory upon every village, even if there are only four in it." By "villages" he means cities. This is not sound from al-Zuhri.

In another narration: "The Friday prayer is obligatory upon the people of every village, even if they are only three, the fourth of them being their imam." Al-Zuhri's hearing from al-Dawsiyyah is not sound. And al-Hukm [[al-Hukm is al-Hukm ibn 'Abd Allah, one of the narrators in the chain of this hadith.]] [[The addition is from al-Daraqutni.]] is abandoned (matruk).

The third issue: The Friday prayer is valid without the permission of the ruler (imam) and without his presence. Abu Hanifah said: Among its conditions is the imam or his deputy. Our evidence is that al-Walid ibn 'Uqbah, the governor of Kufah, was late one day, so Ibn Mas'ud led the people in prayer without his permission. It is also related that 'Ali led the Friday prayer on the day 'Uthman was besieged, and it is not transmitted that he sought his permission. It is related that when Sa'id ibn al-'As, governor of Madinah, left Madinah, Abu Musa led the people in the Friday prayer without seeking permission.

Malik said: Indeed Allah has obligations on His earth which He does not neglect, whether a governor is in charge of them or not.

The fourth issue: Our scholars said: among the conditions for performing it is a roofed mosque. Ibn al-'Arabi said: I do not know its basis.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 62, verse 11 (part 2 of 3):

I say: its basis is His saying, "Purify My House for those who circle it" (22:26), and His saying, "In houses which Allah has permitted to be raised" (24:36). The true meaning of a house (bayt) is that it has walls and a roof. This is the common usage, and Allah knows best.

The fifth issue: His saying, ﴿And they left you standing﴾ is a basis for the requirement that the preacher stand on the pulpit (minbar) when he delivers the sermon (khutbah). 'Alqamah said: 'Abd Allah was asked, "Did the Prophet ﷺ deliver the sermon standing or sitting?" He replied, "Do you not recite, 'And they left you standing'?"

In Sahih Muslim, from Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah, that he entered the mosque while 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Umm al-Hakam was delivering the sermon seated. He said, "Look at this wretched man, delivering the sermon seated, when Allah the Exalted says: ﴿But when they saw a trade or a diversion, they dispersed to it and left you standing﴾ (62:11)."

Al-Tirmidhi (or another compiler) also related from Jabir that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to deliver the sermon standing, then sit, then stand and deliver it. So whoever tells you that he used to deliver the sermon seated has lied. By Allah, I prayed with him more than two thousand prayers.

This is the view of the majority of jurists and leading scholars. Abu Hanifah said: standing is not a condition for it.

It is related that the first to deliver the sermon seated was Mu'awiyah, and that 'Uthman delivered it standing until he grew weak, and then he delivered it seated. It has also been said that Mu'awiyah only delivered it seated because of his age.

The Prophet ﷺ used to deliver the sermon standing, then sit, then stand, and he would not speak while seated. This was related by Jabir ibn Samurah. Ibn 'Umar related it in the Sahih of al-Bukhari.

The sixth issue: the sermon is a condition for the validity of the Friday congregational prayer (Jumu'ah); it is not valid without it. This is the view of the majority of scholars. Al-Hasan said it is recommended (mustahabb). Similarly Ibn al-Majishun said it is a sunnah (a prescribed practice) and not an obligation (fard). Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it has the status of the two rak'ahs of the noon prayer. If someone omits it and performs the Friday prayer, he has omitted the two rak'ahs of the noon prayer.

The evidence for its obligation is His saying, ﴿And they left you standing﴾. This is a rebuke, and what is obligatory is that whose omission is rebuked by the Shari'ah. Furthermore, the Prophet ﷺ never performed it except with a sermon.

The seventh issue: the preacher may lean on a bow or a staff while delivering the sermon. In Sunan Ibn Majah: he said, "Hisham ibn 'Ammar related to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'd ibn 'Ammar ibn Sa'd related to us, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he delivered a sermon in war, delivered it leaning on a bow, and when he delivered a sermon on Friday, he delivered it leaning on a staff."

The eighth issue: when he ascends the pulpit, the preacher gives the greeting of peace to the people, according to al-Shafi'i and others. Malik did not hold this view. Ibn Majah related from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah that the Prophet ﷺ, when he ascended the pulpit, would give the greeting of peace.

The ninth issue: if he delivers the sermon, whether all of it or part of it, without being in a state of ritual purity (tahara), he has acted improperly according to Malik, but he does not need to repeat it if he prays in a state of purity. Al-Shafi'i had two opinions regarding the obligation of purity: he made it a condition in his later (jadid) view and did not make it a condition in his earlier (qadim) view. This is also the view of Abu Hanifah.

The tenth issue: the minimum that suffices in the sermon is that he praises Allah, invokes blessings upon His Prophet ﷺ, exhorts (people) to fear Allah, and recites a verse of the Qur'an. In the second sermon, four things are obligatory like the first, except that what is obligatory in place of reciting a verse in the first is supplication (du'a'), according to most jurists. Abu Hanifah said: if he limits himself to praising (Allah), or glorifying (tasbih) Him, or magnifying (takbir) Him, it suffices.

It is related from 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, that he ascended the pulpit and said, "Al-hamdu lillah," and then became confused. He said, "Abu Bakr and 'Umar used to prepare a speech for this occasion, but you need an effective leader more than you need an eloquent speaker. Sermons will come to you." Then he descended and prayed. This happened in the presence of the Companions, and no one objected to him.

Abu Yusuf and Muhammad said: what is obligatory is whatever falls under the name of a sermon (khutbah). This is also the view of al-Shafi'i. Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: this is the most sound of what has been said on this matter.

The eleventh issue: in Sahih Muslim, from Ya'la ibn Umayyah, that he heard the Prophet ﷺ recite on the pulpit, ﴿And they will call, "O Malik!"﴾ (43:77). And in the same (collection), from 'Amrah bint 'Abd al-Rahman, from a sister of 'Amrah, who said: "I learned Surah Qaf, ﴿Qaf. By the glorious Qur'an﴾ (50:1), only from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on Friday, as he recited it on the pulpit every Friday." It has already passed at the beginning of (the commentary on) Surah Qaf.

In the Maratil of Abu Dawud, from al-Zuhri, who said: the opening of the Prophet's ﷺ sermon was: "All praise is due to Allah. We praise Him, seek His help, and ask His forgiveness, and we seek refuge in Him from the evils of our souls. Whomever Allah guides, none can misguide; and whomever He misguides, none can guide. We bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, whom He sent with the truth as a bringer of good news and a warner before the Hour. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has been rightly guided, and whoever disobeys them has gone astray. We ask Allah, our Lord, to make us among those who obey Him and obey His Messenger, who seek His pleasure and avoid His wrath, for we are His and to Him we belong."

From him (al-Zuhri) also: "We have been told that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say when he delivered a sermon: 'Everything that is to come is near, and there is no distance for what is coming. Allah does not hasten because of anyone's haste, nor does He hurry for the affairs of people. (It is) what Allah wills, not what people will. Allah wills a matter and people will another matter; what Allah wills comes to pass, even if people dislike it. There is no distancing of what Allah has brought near, and no bringing near of what Allah has distanced. Nothing happens except by the permission of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'"

Jabir said: On Friday the Prophet ﷺ used to deliver the sermon, and after praising Allah and invoking blessings upon His prophets, he would say: "O people! Indeed you have landmarks, so proceed to your landmarks. Indeed you have an end, so proceed to your end. Indeed the believing servant is between two fears: between a term that has passed, not knowing what Allah will decree concerning it, and a term that remains, not knowing what Allah will do concerning it. So let the servant take from himself for himself, from his worldly life for his Hereafter, from youth before old age, and from life before death. By Him in whose hand is my soul, after death there is no returning to make amends, and after this world there is no abode except Paradise or Hellfire. I say these words of mine and I ask Allah's forgiveness for myself and for you."

The sermon with which the prayer and peace of Allah be upon him delivered at his first Friday (prayer) upon his arrival in Medina has already been mentioned.

The twelfth issue: silence during the sermon is obligatory upon those who hear it, as a sunnah-level obligation. The sunnah is that whoever hears it and whoever does not hear it should remain silent for it, and both are, if Allah wills, equal in reward. Whoever speaks at that time has engaged in idle talk (laghw), but his prayer is not invalidated by it.

In the Sahih, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "If you say to your companion, 'Be silent,' on Friday while the imam is delivering the sermon, you have engaged in idle talk."

Al-Zamakhshari said: If the one who is silent says to his companion "Shh!", he has engaged in idle talk. Would not the preacher who exaggerates in this matter be engaging in idle talk? We seek refuge in Allah from the strangeness of Islam and the hardship of the times.

The thirteenth issue: the people face the imam when he ascends the pulpit, based on what Abu Dawud related in a mursal report from Aban ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: "I was with 'Adi ibn Thabit on Friday, and when the imam came out, or he said ascended the pulpit, he faced him and said, 'This is how the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to act toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.'" Ibn Majah narrated it from 'Adi ibn Thabit, from his father, adding to the chain: "from his father, who said: when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood on the pulpit, his Companions faced him with their faces." Ibn Majah said: "I hope that it is connected (muttasil)."

I say: Abu Nu'aym al-Hafiz related: "Muhammad ibn Ma'mar related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Najiyah related to us, saying: 'Abbad ibn Ya'qub related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Khurasani related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, from 'Abd Allah, who said: 'When the Prophet ﷺ settled on the pulpit, we faced him with our faces.'" Muhammad ibn al-Fadl ibn 'Atiyyah alone transmitted it from Mansur.

The fourteenth issue: the one who enters the mosque while the imam is delivering the sermon should not perform the bowing prayer (rak'ah) according to Malik, may Allah have mercy on him. This is also the view of Ibn Shihab, may Allah have mercy on him, and others. In the Muwatta' from him (Malik): "The imam's coming out cuts off the prayer, and his speech cuts off (other) speech." This is a mursal report.

In the Sahih of Muslim, from the hadith of Jabir, from the Prophet ﷺ: "When one of you comes on Friday while the imam is delivering the sermon, let him pray two rak'ahs and let him make them brief (tajawwaz)." That is, let him perform them quickly. This is explicit about the bowing prayer, and al-Shafi'i and others hold this view.

The fifteenth issue: ..... [blank in manuscript A] ..... Ibn 'Awn related from Ibn Sirin, who said: "They used to dislike sleeping while the imam was delivering the sermon, and they would speak harshly about it." Ibn 'Awn said: "Afterwards he met me and said, 'Do you know what they say?' He said, 'They say: Their case is like that of a military detachment that failed.' Then he said, 'Do you know what "failed" means? They gained no booty.'"

It is related from Samurah ibn Jundub that the Prophet ﷺ said: "When one of you feels drowsy, let him move to the seat of his companion, and let his companion move to his seat."

SIXTEENTH: Here we mention what we have not mentioned concerning the virtue of the Friday (jumu'ah) prayer and its obligation. The imams narrated from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned the day of Friday and said: "In it there is an hour in which no Muslim servant who is praying and asking Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for something will coincide with it except that He gives it to him." He indicated with his hand, making it small [[i.e., he indicated the shortness of that hour and that it does not extend.]]. In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Abu Musa, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "It is from when the imam sits down until the prayer is concluded." It is also narrated from the hadith of Anas that the Prophet (ﷺ) was delayed from us one day, and when he came out we said: "You were detained!" He said: "That is because Jibril came to me like a white mirror in which there was a black spot. I said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'This is the Friday, in which there is good for you and for your community. The Jews and the Christians wanted it, but they missed it, and Allah guided you to it.' I said: 'O Jibril, what is this black spot?' He said: 'This is the hour that is on the day of Friday. No Muslim servant who asks Allah for good in it coincides with it except that He gives it to him, or stores up for him its like on the Day of Resurrection, or averts from him evil of its like. It is the best of days with Allah, and the people of Paradise call it the Day of Increase.'" He mentioned the hadith. Ibn al-Mubarak and Yahya ibn Sallam both reported: Al-Mas'udi narrated to us from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Abu 'Ubaydah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Utbah, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Hasten to the Friday, for Allah, blessed and exalted, manifests Himself to the people of Paradise every Friday in a sand dune [[al-kathib: a long, elongated heap of sand.]] of white camphor, and they will be near Him according to the measure of their haste to the Friday in the world." Ibn al-Mubarak said: "according to their haste..." and Yahya ibn Sallam said: "like their haste to the Friday in the world." He added: "Then He gives them some honor they had not seen before." Yahya said: "I heard someone other than al-Mas'udi add to it: this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and with Us is more﴾ [Qaf: 35]." [[See vol. 17, p. 21.]]. I say: His saying "in a sand dune" means the people of Paradise, i.e., while they are on a sand dune, as Hasan narrated, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The people of Paradise look at their Lord every Friday from a sand dune of camphor, whose edges cannot be seen, and in it there is a flowing river whose banks are musk. Upon it are female attendants who recite the Qur'an with the most beautiful voices ever heard by the first and the last. When they depart to their dwellings, each man takes by the hand whichever of them he wishes, then they pass over bridges of pearls to their dwellings. Were it not that Allah guides them to their dwellings, they would not find their way to them, because of what Allah renews for them every Friday." Yahya ibn Sallam recorded it. And from Anas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I saw beneath the Throne seventy cities, each city like your cities [[In: H, S, T, L, H: "like your world."]], seventy times over, filled with angels who glorify Allah, sanctify Him, and say in their glorification: 'O Allah, forgive whoever attended the Friday. O Allah, forgive whoever bathed on the day of Friday.'" Al-Tha'labi recorded it. The noble judge Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn 'Abdullah ibn Ibrahim al-Hashimi al-'Isawi, from the descendants of 'Isa ibn 'Ali ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him), also narrated with a sound chain from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will resurrect the days on the Day of Resurrection in their form, and He will resurrect the Friday radiant and luminous, its people encircling it like a bride who is brought to her noble husband. It illuminates for them and they walk in its light. Their complexions are whiter than snow, their scent spreads like musk. They wade through mountains of camphor. The two weighty creatures [[jinn and humankind]] look at them in amazement, and they do not blink. They enter Paradise, and none mixes with them except the muezzins who seek reward [[i.e., those who seek the face of Allah and His reward.]]." In the Sunan of Ibn Majah, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "From one Friday to the next is an expiation for what is between them, so long as major sins are not committed." Muslim recorded it with a similar meaning. And from Aws ibn Aws al-Thaqafi, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever washes on the day of Friday, bathes, goes early and arrives early, walks and does not ride, draws near to the imam and listens, and does not engage in idle talk, will have for each step the reward of a year's fasting and standing in prayer." From Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) addressed us and said: "O people, repent to Allah before you die. Hasten to good deeds before you are preoccupied. Maintain your bond with your Lord by frequently remembering Him and by much charity, in secret and in public, so that you may be provided for, helped, and rewarded. Know that Allah has made the Friday obligatory upon you in this place of mine, in this month of mine, in this year of mine, until the Day of Resurrection. Whoever abandons it during my lifetime or after my death, whether the ruler is just or unjust, out of contempt for it or denial of it, then may Allah not gather his affairs and not bless his undertakings. Beware: he has no prayer, no zakat, no hajj. Beware: he has no fast and no righteousness until he repents, and whoever repents, Allah will accept his repentance. Beware: no woman should lead a man in prayer, no Bedouin should lead an emigrant, and no wicked person should lead a believer, unless he is compelled by a ruler whose sword or whip he fears." Maymun ibn Abi Shaybah said: "I wanted to attend the Friday prayer with al-Hajjaj, so I prepared to go. Then I said: 'Where am I going? Shall I pray behind this wicked man?' Once I said: 'I will go,' and once: 'I will not go.' Then I resolved to go, and a caller called out to me from the side of the house: ﴿O you who believe, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trading﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 9]." SEVENTEENTH: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: What is with Allah is better than diversion and than trade﴾. There are two interpretations concerning it. The first: what is with Allah of reward for your prayer is better than the pleasure of your diversion and the profit of your trade. The second: what is with Allah of your provision, which He has apportioned to you, is better than what you obtain from your diversion and your trade. Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi recited: ﴿Say: What is with Allah is better than diversion and than trade, for those who believe﴾.
(﴿And Allah is the best of providers﴾) That is, the best of those who provide and give. So from Him seek, and seek help through obedience to Him in attaining what He has of the good of this world and the Hereafter.
